question: Does a creature with haste still have summoning sickness for tapping abilities?
expected_answer: No. Haste lets the creature ignore the summoning sickness rule entirely: it can attack AND activate abilities whose cost includes the tap or untap symbol even if it hasn't been under its controller's control since their most recent turn began (rule 702.10c).
source: https://reddit.com/r/askajudge/... (expected_answer corrected 2026-06-09: original wrongly claimed haste doesn't lift the tap-ability restriction, contradicting CR 702.10c)

question: I cast Lightning Bolt targeting my opponent's 3/3 creature. My opponent responds with Giant Growth on that creature. Does the creature survive?
expected_answer: Yes. Giant Growth resolves first (last in, first out on the stack), giving the creature +3/+3 and making it a 6/6. Lightning Bolt then resolves and deals 3 damage — not enough to destroy a 6/6 with 6 toughness. The creature survives.
source: drafted by Claude Code, reviewed by user

question: I tap Llanowar Elves for green mana. In response, my opponent casts Lightning Bolt targeting the Elves. Do I still get the mana?
expected_answer: Yes. Tapping Llanowar Elves for mana is a mana ability, which doesn't use the stack and resolves immediately. The mana is added to your mana pool before your opponent can respond. Lightning Bolt can then be cast and will destroy the Elves, but you keep the mana.
source: drafted by Claude Code, reviewed by user

question: Can I target my own creature with Path to Exile to search my library for a basic land?
expected_answer: Yes. Path to Exile says 'target creature' with no restriction on controller. You can target your own creature. It will be exiled and you get to search for a basic land.
source: drafted by Claude Code, reviewed by user

question: A creature with deathtouch deals 1 damage to a 5/5 creature with no other abilities. Does the 5/5 die?
expected_answer: Yes. State-based actions check whether a creature has been dealt damage by a source with deathtouch since the last time state-based actions were checked. Any amount of deathtouch damage is enough to destroy a creature, regardless of its toughness.
source: drafted by Claude Code, reviewed by user

question: A token creature is dealt lethal damage and dies. Does it go to the graveyard before ceasing to exist?
expected_answer: Yes. The token goes to the graveyard as a state-based action, triggering any 'when a creature dies' effects. It then ceases to exist as a state-based action because tokens can't exist in zones other than the battlefield.
source: drafted by Claude Code, reviewed by user

question: My attacking creature has first strike and the blocking creature doesn't. How is combat damage dealt?
expected_answer: There are two combat damage steps. In the first, only creatures with first strike or double strike assign damage, so your attacker deals its damage first. If that damage destroys the blocker, the blocker is no longer on the battlefield in the second combat damage step and deals no combat damage at all.

question: Can my white creature block an attacking creature that has protection from white?
expected_answer: No. Attacking creatures with protection can't be blocked by creatures that have the stated quality, so a white creature can't block a creature with protection from white.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My creature has hexproof. Can I still target it with my own spells?
expected_answer: Yes. Hexproof only says the permanent can't be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control. Your own spells and abilities can target it normally.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: I cast Clone copying a creature that has three +1/+1 counters on it. Does my Clone enter the battlefield with those counters?
expected_answer: No. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original's characteristics (name, types, power/toughness as printed, abilities, etc.). Counters are not copiable values, so Clone enters as the original creature's printed version without the +1/+1 counters.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: If an effect copies a spell on the stack, is the copy considered to have been cast? Will abilities that trigger 'whenever a player casts a spell' trigger for it?
expected_answer: No. A copy of a spell is created directly on the stack — it isn't cast. Abilities that trigger on casting a spell won't trigger for the copy. The copy still resolves like a normal spell.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My opponent controls a permanent saying that if a creature would die, it's exiled instead. My creature with a 'when this creature dies' ability is destroyed. Does its ability trigger?
expected_answer: No. A replaced event never happens — the creature is exiled directly from the battlefield instead of going to the graveyard, so it never dies ('dies' means put into a graveyard from the battlefield), and the dies trigger doesn't trigger.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: Earlier this turn my 3/3 creature got +3/+3 from Giant Growth. Now an effect makes it 'become 0/2 until end of turn'. What are its power and toughness?
expected_answer: It's a 3/5. Effects that SET power/toughness to specific numbers apply in layer 7b, and effects that MODIFY power/toughness like +3/+3 apply later, in layer 7c — regardless of which effect has the earlier timestamp. So the creature becomes 0/2, then +3/+3 is applied on top, giving 3/5.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My 2/2 creature gets -2/-2 from a spell. Can I regenerate it to save it?
expected_answer: No. A creature with toughness 0 or less is put into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action, and regeneration explicitly can't replace this event — regeneration only replaces destruction.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: I control a legendary creature and cast a second copy of the same legendary creature. What happens?
expected_answer: When the second one enters the battlefield, the legend rule applies: as a state-based action you choose one of them to keep, and the other is put into its owner's graveyard.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: Can I cast a sorcery during my opponent's turn?
expected_answer: No, not normally. Sorceries can only be cast during your own main phase, when the stack is empty and you have priority. Only effects that explicitly allow it (e.g. granting flash) change this.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My creature has 'When this creature dies, draw a card.' When it dies, can my opponent respond to that trigger?
expected_answer: Yes. Once it triggers, the ability is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, and players can respond to it like any other ability on the stack (e.g. with an ability-countering spell). The creature itself is already dead regardless.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: If I add mana to my mana pool and don't spend it before the phase ends, do I lose life from mana burn?
expected_answer: No. Mana burn no longer exists in the rules. Unspent mana simply empties from your mana pool at the end of each step and phase with no penalty.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: I block a 5/5 attacker with my 1/1, and my opponent destroys my 1/1 before combat damage. Does the 5/5 deal its damage to me?
expected_answer: No. The 5/5 is still a blocked creature, and a blocked creature with no creatures currently blocking it assigns no combat damage (unless it has trample or an ability like that). You take no damage.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: How many lands can I play per turn, and when can I play them?
expected_answer: Normally one land per turn, during your own main phase when the stack is empty and you have priority. Playing a land is a special action that doesn't use the stack. Continuous effects can increase the number.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: I have 9 cards in hand at the end of my turn. What happens?
expected_answer: During your cleanup step you discard down to your maximum hand size (normally seven), so you discard two cards. This turn-based action doesn't use the stack.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My creature has three +1/+1 counters on it and an effect puts two -1/-1 counters on it. What happens to the counters?
expected_answer: As a state-based action, +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters annihilate in pairs: two of each are removed, leaving the creature with a single +1/+1 counter.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: I cast a spell targeting a single creature, and my opponent sacrifices that creature in response. What happens to my spell?
expected_answer: When your spell tries to resolve, it checks its targets. The creature is no longer in the zone it was targeted in, so it's an illegal target. With all of its targets illegal, the spell doesn't resolve and is put into its owner's graveyard, having no effect. (Informally, it 'fizzles'.)
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My opponent's creature has ward {2}. I cast Murder targeting it but I don't pay the ward cost. What happens?
expected_answer: Ward is a triggered ability: when the creature becomes the target of your spell, ward triggers, and Murder is countered unless you pay {2}. If you decline to pay, Murder is countered and the creature survives.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My 4/4 attacker has both deathtouch and trample. My opponent blocks with a 5/5. How much damage can I assign to the defending player?
expected_answer: You can assign 3 damage to the player. With trample you must assign lethal damage to the blocker first, but because the attacker has deathtouch, any nonzero damage counts as lethal for this purpose. So you can assign just 1 damage to the 5/5 (which will destroy it via deathtouch) and the remaining 3 to the defending player.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: My indestructible 1/1 creature gets -1/-1 until end of turn. Does it die?
expected_answer: Yes. Indestructible only prevents destruction. A creature with toughness 0 or less is put into its owner's graveyard as a state-based action — that's not destruction, so indestructible doesn't save it.
source: drafted by Claude Code (Fable 5), pending user review

question: Can I cast a creature with flash during my opponent's combat phase?
expected_answer: Yes. Flash means you may cast the spell any time you could cast an instant, so you can cast it whenever you have priority, including during your opponent's combat phase.
